description.summary: publish and invoke a window's application commands

protocol.description:
A running application publishes its own commands and recent items to the shell. Invocation is delivered to the owning window, never interpreted as a shell command or used to start a process. Each window registers separately so its commands address that window's current document, tab, or focused pane.
This protocol does not reserve global shortcuts. Shortcut strings are display hints for bindings implemented by the application or compositor.

description.summary: register commands for an owned xdg_toplevel

entry.name: already_registered
entry.summary: this toplevel already has a registration

entry.name: invalid_toplevel
entry.summary: the toplevel is not owned by this client

description.summary: release the manager without removing registrations

request.name: get_commands

description.summary: create a registration for this client's window

request.description: At most one registration may exist for an xdg_toplevel. Registration starts empty. It remains associated with the xdg_toplevel across unmap and remap, but commands cannot be invoked while the window is unmapped. Destroying the xdg_toplevel closes the registration. Other windows, including windows of the same application, are unaffected.

interface.name: kora_app_commands_handle_v1

description.summary: an atomic command catalog for one window

interface.description:
Catalog requests modify pending state. Done applies that state atomically; until then the shell displays the last committed catalog. After done, pending state starts as a copy of the committed state. Clear followed by additions and done replaces the entire catalog without a visible empty interval. Destroy removes both pending and committed state immediately.
Strings are UTF-8. IDs are 1 to 128 ASCII bytes using letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens. Labels are 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes; optional shortcut, section, icon and sublabel strings may be empty and are at most 256 bytes. Invalid strings, unknown IDs and invalid flags are protocol errors. A catalog contains at most 256 application commands.

entry.name: invalid_value
entry.summary: a value violates the catalog contract

entry.name: reserved_id
entry.summary: an application command shadows a system command

entry.name: unknown_id
entry.summary: a state update names an undeclared command

entry.name: menu
entry.summary: nominate this command for the compact app menu

entry.name: stateful
entry.summary: the command has an active state

entry.name: bound
entry.summary: the application implements the advertised shortcut

description.summary: remove the registration and its catalog
empty the pending commands, handled verbs and recent items

request.name: handle

description.summary: handle a standard application or editing verb

request.description: Allowed IDs are undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, selall, markv, settings, neww, find and info. Their labels, groups and shortcut hints belong to the shell. The application declares whether it can currently perform the verb. Enabled is either zero or one. Repeated declarations replace the previous declaration. Capture and window-management verbs cannot be intercepted through this request.

request.name: add_command

description.summary: add or replace a named application command

request.description: An application command ID must contain a dot, such as term.clear, and cannot use a standard command ID. Replacing a command keeps its original order, enables it and resets its active state to false. The shell offers at most the first six menu nominees, in declaration order. Other commands remain available in the palette. Icon is a symbolic icon name, never a file path; an unsupported or empty name uses the generic command glyph.

request.name: set_state

description.summary: set a stateful application's command state

request.description: Active is zero or one. The command must already exist and have the stateful flag. This affects presentation; it does not invoke the command.

request.name: set_enabled
request.description: Enabled is zero or one. The application command must already exist. Disabled commands remain discoverable but cannot be invoked or pinned.

request.name: add_recent
request.description: ID is meaningful only to this registration; it is never resolved as a file path or URI by the compositor. Repeated IDs replace previous items. The timestamp is unsigned milliseconds since the Unix epoch, encoded as (timestamp_hi shifted left by 32) plus timestamp_lo. The shell retains at most the ten newest entries in both pending and committed state, breaking ties by declaration order. Additional older items are discarded immediately. Open Recent is displayed only when this set is nonempty.

request.name: done
request.description: Generation identifies this catalog revision and is echoed with every invocation. The client must choose a different generation for each commit and ignore invocations from catalogs it no longer handles. The compositor must discard a shell selection if the generation captured when that menu or palette was built differs from the current catalog, even if the selected ID still exists. It must also recheck command presence and enabled state, or recent-item presence, before sending an invocation. This applies to both invoke and recent_selected.

request.name: request_palette

description.summary: open the shell palette for this focused window

request.description: The compositor may honor this request only while this mapped toplevel has keyboard focus on the given seat and serial names a recent input event actually delivered to this client for that seat and window. Stale or foreign serials and requests from background, hidden or parked windows are ignored.

event.name: invoke

description.summary: perform a command in this window

event.description: ID names an enabled command or handled standard verb in the committed generation. Serial identifies the triggering shell input, not a grant of access to another window or workspace. The application performs the action and publishes any resulting state through a later done.

event.name: recent_selected

description.summary: open a recent item in this window

event.description: The application resolves its own opaque ID and handles missing or stale content. The compositor does not read the item or execute its ID.

event.name: closed
event.description: The registration is inert, its catalog has been removed, and no more events follow. The client should destroy the handle. Requests other than destroy are ignored after closed.
